facts.text: I said this is part 17 of my multiple messages.
I said the Master erred in the approach he adopted.
I said the integrity of the entire levee system is a matter of great importance to the town of Brewarrina.
I said a whole levee bank might be breached by water penetration around a culvert.
I said a levee might fail at any location where fill is sufficiently loose or cracks are sufficiently deep.
I said Professor Fell, an expert witness for the Council, testified that only one layer of poorly compacted soil might give a path for seepage and initiation of erosion.
I said the relevance of the contractual requirements for testing at the culverts is self-evident.
I said the purpose of the testing requirements was to give an appropriate degree of satisfaction to the Council as to the quality of the work done and the integrity of the system.
I accepted Beckhaus’s submission that failure to carry out some tests does not necessarily mean the completed works do not substantially comply with the contractual standard.

I said that once it is established there has been a failure to comply with the testing requirements, the evidentiary onus passes to Beckhaus to provide other evidence to the same degree of assurance as satisfactory test results would have provided.
I said the assurance could be derived from tests carried out subsequently or from some other source, and that Beckhaus would need to establish it.
I said Beckhaus failed to comply with the obligation to add 3% lime to all material.
I said the failure to add 3% lime gives rise to at least a prima facie doubt that the levees had the qualities that the addition of lime to that extent would achieve.
I said compaction tests known as “CETS” were performed while Beckhaus was carrying out work under the Contract in circumstances that cast some doubt on the conclusions from the results.
I said some 340 CETS tests were carried out in random places relating to compaction levels on the levee system.
I said all those 340 CETS tests passed.
I said Beckhaus submitted that the CETS results alone provided a high degree of assurance that contractual standards had been met generally.
I said some CETS tests only passed after the persons testing indicated to Beckhaus that a test at the particular place was likely to fail.
I said Beckhaus then added lime and reworked the area before the test was carried out and passed successfully.
I said Mr Rudge explained that the CETS testers did not issue failing certificates.
I said the CETS testers were sufficiently experienced to tell on site that something was not properly compacted because of deleterious material within the area and that it would fail.
I said the CETS testers would tell the foreman that the area was not going to pass, and the foreman would arrange for it to be reworked.
I said after reworking, an adjacent or nearby area would be retested.
I said if it looked as if it was going to pass, the sample was then taken back to the laboratory and generally it did.
I said this practice detracts from the degree of assurance that successful CETS testing would otherwise have provided.
I said these two matters emphasise the need for Beckhaus to rebut the inference arising from failure to provide satisfactory test results required by cl 3.8 and cl 8.9.3 of the specification.

I said the mere fact that compaction was actually performed at culverts does not provide the degree of assurance that would have been forthcoming had satisfactory tests been carried out at the frequency required by the Contract.
I said the Master erred in finding that the evidence demonstrated substantial compliance with the contractual requirements for compaction over the culverts.
I said the Council is entitled to damages flowing from breach of contract arising from failure to carry out tests required in relation to compaction at the culverts.
I said the damages are the costs of rectifying the work at the culverts.
I said rectification would involve removing the fill over and in the vicinity of the culverts sufficiently to enable the work to be done in accordance with the contract.
I proposed that the assessment of such damages should be remitted to Macready AsJ.

events.text: Proposed remitting the assessment of damages to Macready AsJ.
